title: kv-reshard-maintenance-triggering-intermittent-5xx-and-sdk-retry-amplification
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a planned KV shard rebalance (rolling maintenance of node pool A->B) we observed intermittent 5xx responses for a small subset of tenants. The error pattern correlated with shard move windows and coincided with an enterprise customer (NimbusAI) opening an escalation because their SDK clients experienced hard failures instead of graceful retries. Root problem appears to be a race across three systems: router routing table propagation, in-flight KV cache state on serving nodes, and overly-aggressive SDK retry semantics that immediately reissued requests to hot targets. This ticket coordinates a short-term mitigation for customer-visible errors, a patch to server-side admission/backoff behavior, and a follow-up to harden maintenance flows so rebalances do not induce transient 5xx spikes.
steps_reproduced: Schedule a small rolling maintenance that drains 1/6th of serving nodes in a cluster for KV re-sharding
Observe that router updates lag manifest write by ~3-12s for some edge proxies (trace id pattern trace_xxx)
Issue a stream of requests from an SDK client configured with instant retry (no jitter, zero base backoff)
See served nodes return 500/502 when they encounter partial KV state and cannot reconstruct KV-cache entries during warmup
Concurrent retries concentrate on newly promoted hot shards and push the node over its request admission thresholds, causing further 5xx until delay triggers fallback
recent_updates: 2026-03-10: Pager alerted SRE after NimbusAI reported 15% error rate spike; on-call (Miguel) opened this ticket and started triage
2026-03-10: Canary rollback of the maintenance window reduced errors but did not fully eliminate spikes; root cause narrowed to routing + cache warmup race
2026-03-11: Added temporary tenant-level admission cap (soft cap = 4x normal) for NimbusAI while investigating; customer acknowledged reduced impact
2026-03-12: Engineering reproduced locally using synthetic battched load and SDK emulator. Observed immediate retry amplification when client retry backoff = 0ms
2026-03-13: Code patch candidate (PR #10427) introduces server-side request admission hysteresis + transient-backoff header to advise SDKs
2026-03-14: PM (Emily Chen) approved staged rollout. Support sent NimbusAI runbook for temporary SDK config change (enable exponential jitter).
mitigation_actions: Applied tenant soft admission caps for affected customers (runbook id RB-2026-19)
Disabled aggressive rebalancing for next 48h and switched to 10s staggered drains
Pushed heuristic in edge router to prefer nodes with fresh kv-cache when available (config toggle on: router.kv_prefer_fresh=true)
Guided NimbusAI to enable exponential backoff + jitter in their SDK; provided sample patch and command to flip a feature flag
Opened a temporary fallback route for critical tenants to a read-only cache-backed path to reduce load on hot nodes
root_cause_summary: A timing window during KV shard reallocation exposed a race where router manifest updates propagated slower than node drain state, causing some requests to hit nodes with partially reconstructed KV caches. Those nodes returned transient 5xx while warming. Customer SDKs with zero-backoff retry semantics immediately retried hotspots, amplifying the load and pushing admission logic to return 5xx at scale. Lack of server-side advisory headers and no temporary tenant shaping during maintenance made the spike customer-visible.
fix_candidates: Config change: router.kv_prefer_fresh=true applied to region-us-west-2 (temporary)
rollout_plan: Canary 1: deploy PR #10427 to canary serving pool in us-west-2 with +10% traffic for 2 hours
Canary 2: enable router.kv_prefer_fresh=true for canary proxies and monitor ERR5xx and latencies for 4 hours
Gradual: if canaries stable, roll to 25%/50%/100% of serving pool within 24h with rollback gates on ERR5xx > 1.5x baseline
Customer safe path: keep tenant soft caps for NimbusAI for 72 hours post-rollout and coordinate SDK guidance
Post-rollout: schedule maintenance-runbook update and add automated preflight checks for stale-manifest-lag
monitoring_queries: Errors per minute by node: sum(rate(serving_errors_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) by (node)
KV cache miss & warmup: sum(rate(kv_cache_rebuilds_total[1m])) by (shard)
Alert: kv_rebalance_ongoing AND router_manifest_lag > 5s AND (ERR5xx_rate > baseline*1.2)
postmortem_todo: Finalize postmortem write-up with timeline and attach customer comms (owner: Miguel)
Add automated preflight check to abort rebalance if router_manifest_lag 99p > 5s
Enhance SDK docs and add a recommended default backoff/jitter if using synchronous retries
Create a maintenance-mode feature that automatically applies tenant soft caps during rebalances
Run a chaos test that simulates stale router manifests and validate protection logic
